# Scenarist

> Scenarist is a professional screenwriting app for iPhone and iPad. It writes and formats screenplays to industry standard, works fully offline with no account, and includes voice dictation that formats a script as you speak. Built for both traditional screenwriters (feature film, TV) and YouTube / short-form video creators.

Platform: iOS 18.2 and later (iPhone and iPad)
Developer: Mykola Viunyk (independent)
Website: https://scenaristapp.com
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6762529535

## What it does

Scenarist replaces desktop screenwriting software on the phone. Unlike tools that add a mobile view to a desktop app, it is designed phone-first: auto-formatting happens as you type, so you never stop to set margins or change styles. It requires no account, no login, and no internet connection.

## Free features

Free is not a trial. There is no time limit and no script cap.

- Industry-standard screenplay auto-formatting: scene heading, action, character, dialogue, parenthetical, transition, shot
- Unlimited scripts
- Export to PDF and Fountain (.fountain)
- Import from Fountain, including title page data
- iCloud sync across devices, no account or signup required
- Outline view and scene navigator
- Find and replace
- Dual dialogue
- Focus mode
- Recently Deleted with 30-day recovery
- Templates: feature film, TV drama, TV comedy, YouTube long-form, short-form video
- Per-element voice dictation: say "interior coffee shop day" and get INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY
- Character and location autocomplete
- Notes and bookmarks

## Pro features (subscription or one-time Lifetime unlock)

- Voice to Script: full hands-free dictation. Speak "scene heading", "character", "dialogue", "action", "parenthetical", or "cut to" to switch element types, and Scenarist formats the screenplay live as you talk. Runs entirely on-device using Apple Speech.
- Final Draft (.fdx) export
- Index cards / beat board with drag-to-reorder, in grid, corkboard and timeline layouts
- Script statistics: page count, scene count, dialogue distribution by character, location breakdown, interior/exterior and day/night ratios
- Revision tracking with the standard production revision colours
- Teleprompter mode: full-screen auto-scroll with adjustable speed and font size, horizontal mirroring, light and dark themes, drag-to-scrub, elapsed timer, and a countdown before recording
- Script preview: paginated, print-ready pages

## Pricing

- Free tier: full writing, formatting, PDF and Fountain export, and iCloud sync. Not time-limited, no script cap.
- Pro monthly: $6.99 USD
- Pro annual: $29.99 USD
- Lifetime: $49.99 USD one-time, no subscription
- Both subscription plans include a 7-day free trial.
- No advertising in any tier.

Prices are US storefront as of August 2026 and vary by region.

## Privacy and data handling

- All script content is stored on the user's device and in their own private iCloud container.
- Speech recognition runs on-device via Apple's Speech framework. Dictation audio is not uploaded to any server.
- There is no Scenarist account system, no login, and no user database.
- No third-party analytics SDKs, no advertising SDKs, no tracking.
- Scripts remain readable, editable, and exportable with no internet connection.

## How it compares

- Versus Final Draft: Scenarist is phone-native and works offline with no subscription required for core writing; Final Draft is the desktop industry standard with deeper production features.
- Versus Fade In: Fade In's mobile app has been discontinued and replaced by Fade In Access, a browser-based service. Scenarist is a native iOS app that works with no connection.
- Versus Slugline and Highland: comparable Fountain fidelity, but those are macOS applications; Scenarist runs on iPhone and iPad.
- Versus WriterDuet and Arc Studio: those centre on real-time cloud collaboration; Scenarist centres on solo, offline, local-first writing and voice input.
- Versus Celtx: Celtx covers full production management; Scenarist focuses on writing and formatting.
- Unique to Scenarist: keyword-driven full dictation that produces formatted screenplay pages, plus a teleprompter, plus dedicated YouTube and short-form script modes.
- Known limitations: no real-time collaboration, no desktop or web version, and no Android version.

## Who it is for

- Screenwriters drafting feature films and television on a phone or tablet
- Writers who need a native app that works offline, including on planes and underground transit
- YouTube and short-form creators scripting videos and reading them to camera
- Writers who prefer dictating over typing, including those with RSI or accessibility needs
- Anyone wanting industry-standard formatting without a recurring desktop software licence
